voices.note: the anonymous tanna of the mishna 83a.6-8

props.gloss_en: on four occasions in the year one who sells an animal to his fellow must inform him: I sold its mother to slaughter, I sold its daughter to slaughter
and these are they: the eve of the last festival day of Sukkot, the eve of the first festival day of Pesach, the eve of Shavuot, and the eve of Rosh HaShana
and according to R' Yose HaGelili, also the eve of Yom Kippur in the Galilee
R' Yehuda: when [must he inform]? when he has no interval; but if he has an interval he need not inform him
and R' Yehuda concedes that one who sells the mother to the groom and the daughter to the bride must inform him
for it is known that both of them slaughter on one day
on these four occasions the butcher is made to slaughter against his will: even an ox worth a thousand dinars, and the buyer has only a dinar [in it], he is compelled to slaughter
therefore, if it dies, it dies to [the loss of] the buyer
but on the rest of the days of the year it is not so [the butcher is not compelled]
therefore, [on the rest of the year] if it dies, it dies to [the loss of] the seller

supports.gloss_en: בידוע ששניהם שוחטין ביום אחד -- the groom and bride slaughter on the same day, so the interval does not help
לפיכך -- since the butcher is compelled to slaughter on these occasions, if it dies it dies to the buyer
אינו כן, לפיכך -- on other days there is no such compulsion, therefore if it dies it dies to the seller
